groups.text: It is currently 17 degrees and raining in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

PyTorch is expanding its testing capabilities for Intel XPU hardware to ensure broader compatibility across its software ecosystem. Developers have enabled XPU testing for 46 specific test classes distributed across 37 different test files. This update extends the instantiate device type tests to allow a true value for those confirmed to work on Intel's architecture. To reach this stage, the team validated these classes using pytest filtered specifically for XPU. The results show that 40 of these classes passed successfully. Six other classes timed out because they exceeded the six-hundred-second per-class limit, though they still produced valid XPU rows. However, not every class made the cut. Fifty-three classes were excluded because they produced no XPU rows, while another fifteen were left out due to unexplained failures during the validation process. This targeted expansion ensures that only verified components are integrated into the active testing suite for Intel hardware.

In India’s financial capital of Mumbai, heavy monsoon rains have triggered the collapse of two to three multi-story buildings in a slum area, killing six people. The downpour has forced schools to close and disrupted flight and train schedules, along with traffic on the busy Mumbai-Pune Expressway. Meanwhile, in eastern West Bengal, a mob lynched a suspect after the body of a twelve-year-old girl was found stuffed in a sack on the outskirts of Kolkata. Protesters blocked roads and damaged police vehicles, while authorities have arrested four people in connection with the death. In a different climate, firefighters in southern France are struggling to contain a forest fire near Perpignan that has already destroyed 4,600 hectares. Nearly 10,000 residents were evacuated as flames spread through the Pyrénées-Orientales mountains. Five people, including two firefighters, have been injured during the operation.

Germany is facing a heatwave for the history books after record temperatures hit the country in late June. The German Weather Service reports that 46 measuring stations across eleven federal states surpassed the 40-degree mark, marking the highest temperatures ever documented for the month of June. These intense periods of heat have left many residents unable to find relief or restful sleep in their own homes. Thomas Auer, a professor of building technology at TU Munich, warns that failing to plan for summer cooling during construction is a major error. He notes that while floor-to-ceiling windows provide light, direct sunlight remains the primary source of heat. This creates a dangerous greenhouse atmosphere, particularly in rental apartments and top-floor flats where shutters or blinds are often missing. Because these conditions can lead to severe health consequences or even death, Auer argues that homeowners and municipalities must now rethink and rebuild their housing.

Apple is facing a class action lawsuit from three YouTube channels—h3h3Productions, MrShortGame Golf, and Golfholics—who accuse the company of illegally siphoning videos to train its AI models. The creators claim Apple bypassed technical protections in violation of the DMCA to feed a multi-billion dollar industry without compensation. Similar complaints have been filed against Meta, Snap, ByteDance, and NVIDIA. Meanwhile, Alibaba is banning its employees from using Claude Code at work, citing surveillance risks after discovering functions that could identify Chinese users. Starting July 10, Alibaba staff must use the company's internal platform, Qoder. In a different struggle over resource rights, India has submitted its first national report on the Nagoya Protocol to the UN Convention on Biological Diversity. However, critics argue the report fails to recognize the rights of Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities to give prior informed consent for the use of their traditional knowledge.

The European Space Agency’s Euclid telescope has discovered 31 of the most ancient quasars ever found, including two that are the earliest observed in cosmic history. These dazzling galaxy cores were powered by gargantuan black holes and shone with the light of a trillion suns when the universe was only 670 million years old. Because these objects reveal how the first galaxies took shape, they have been hunted for decades, though their faint primordial light is often confused with closer stars. Shifting to climate efforts on Earth, Katapult Africa has opened applications for its latest accelerator programme targeting early-stage climate-tech startups. The three-month initiative focuses on agritech and resilient food systems across the continent. Participating ventures will receive between 150,000 and 500,000 US dollars in equity investment alongside intensive workshops to help them reach milestones in growth and investor readiness.

Massive crowds of mourners filled the streets of Tehran on Monday morning for the funeral procession of Iran's late supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. State television reported that the event marks the third day of a state funeral designed by the Iranian government to project strength and unity. This display of resilience comes after five weeks of war with Israel and the United States. In eastern Tehran, mourners gathered in Imam Hussein Square and hanged an effigy of US President Donald Trump. While the public gathers, attention remains fixed on Khamenei's successor, his son Mojtaba Khamenei, who has not appeared in public since taking power. The late leader was killed on February 28 during the first day of the Middle East war, and his body began its journey through the capital after lying in state for two days at the Grand Mosalla religious complex.

A Russian shelling attack on Kyiv has destroyed the apartment of media professionals Svitlana Chepurenko and Kateryna Fedorchenko. Both women were in a shelter during the strike and did not suffer any injuries. In separate news from the shipping sector, Geneva-based Advantage Tankers has confirmed two new suezmax crude tankers at Samsung Heavy Industries. Led by Tugrul Tokgoz, the company is commissioning the Advantage Spirit and Advantage Synergy as dual-fuel-ready units. Each vessel costs 88.25 million dollars and carries a capacity of 157,000 deadweight tonnes. These ships are scheduled for delivery in the first and second quarters of 2029, with construction expected to be subcontracted to PaxOcean Zhoushan in China. This order expands a growing fleet that already includes several very large crude carriers under construction at other South Korean and Chinese yards.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will bring rain with temperatures between 17 and 20 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.

On your calendar today: Your work calendar has the AP2 meeting at nine in the morning. Your personal calendar has the BLISS Reading Group at six forty-five in the evening, followed by Twerchhau at seven.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
